newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Rugby League-Warriors asked to freeze negotiations.
newsitem.headline: Rugby League-Warriors asked to freeze negotiations.

text.p: A group bidding to buy the Auckland Warriors has asked the league team not to commit to any new player contracts just yet, former Kiwi coach Graham Lowe said on Tuesday.

Lowe, who is involved with ex-Kiwi Dean Lonergan and public relations group owner Malcom Boyle in a bid to purchase the Auckland club, said his group had asked the Warriors' owners, the Auckland Rugby League, to request the Warriors hold fire on any new contracts until the sale issue is resolved.
"In our view, it doesn't make any sense to be negotiation either new or existing contracts when the future ownership of the club is still unclear," Lowe said.
"Whether it is our group or any other, a new owner may have different ideas about the playing strength of the club in the future."
Lowe said his group was not trying to hinder the club's development, but it would not be fair on anyone it players were signed and then found they were unwanted next season.
He said Auckland Rugby League chairman Sel Bennett confirmed the ARL would speak to the Warriors' board about the matter.
